question.text: What happens to standing instructions (SIP, STP, SWP) when a folio is consolidated with another folio?

answer.text: All standing instructions are automatically cancelled
Standing instructions need to be reviewed and reconfigured for the consolidated folio as per the investor's preference
Standing instructions are automatically merged and amounts are combined
Standing instructions from both folios continue independently

explanation.text: The Logic: Standing instructions like SIP, STP, and SWP are tied to a specific folio's bank mandate, registered amount, frequency, and scheme selection. When folios belonging to the same investor are consolidated into a surviving folio, those mandates cannot be carried over blindly — the investor's preferences for frequency, amount, and which scheme to debit may need updating. Industry operational practice is therefore to review each standing instruction and reconfigure it under the surviving folio per the investor's confirmation, rather than auto-cancel or auto-merge. The Trap: Auto-cancellation would interrupt the investor's investing pattern without consent. Auto-merging amounts could result in unintended doubled debits. Letting both folios' instructions run in parallel after consolidation defeats the purpose of consolidation and creates reconciliation issues. Note: The NISM Series II-B Registrars and Transfer Agents (Mutual Fund) workbook (Dec 2025) covers SIP/STP/SWP mechanics and folio operations but the specific treatment of standing instructions on folio consolidation is not stated on the cited pages (92, 137, 172, 190-193). The framing above is general RTA operational practice.
